ticker.text: Commanders LT Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps in Saturday's practice — surgery required, out most or all of 2026 (ESPN, NFL Network, 8/8)
Josh Downs missed Saturday's Colts practice with a groin injury — the third Colts WR out, alongside Alec Pierce (PUP) and Laquon Treadwell
Raiders held Kirk Cousins and Maxx Crosby out of team drills Saturday after a practice fight — rookie Fernando Mendoza took the first-team reps
DONE — Jahmyr Gibbs signs 3 years, $67.5M with Detroit ($22.5M AAV, $51.5M new guarantees, up to $75.75M) — highest-paid RB in NFL history, passing Bijan

items.text: Fresh window — FFC PPR 12-team ADP, 4,460 mocks 7/28–8/4: Jahmyr Gibbs 1.6, Bijan Robinson 2.0, Puka Nacua 2.7, Ja'Marr Chase 3.9, Christian McCaffrey 5.3, Jaxon Smith-Njigba 5.9, Amon-Ra St. Brown 7.2, Jonathan Taylor 7.6. The pick-3 calculus changed Tuesday: Bijan signed his 3yr/$66.75M extension, so he will not slip. Gibbs is the only unsigned hold-in left and therefore the only realistic RB1 fall to slot 3

Biggest riser in the top 50 and a reversal of last week's read: Malik Nabers moved 41.2 to 34.8 (+6.4). The Giants declined to place him on PUP and he has been ramping up in camp. He is on track for Week 1 per team reporting but has publicly refused to guarantee it — "if my body doesn't feel right, I'm not going to play." No longer a faller; now a mild reach at cost, and a clear buy if he slips past 45

Rashee Rice is the most unsettled price on the board. FFC has him at 11.5 overall (WR6) but on only 123 drafts, while FFPC-style markets had him sliding to the early third after May knee-debris surgery and a 30-day jail term for a probation violation. Andy Reid cleared him for camp and he is practicing. Two markets that far apart means the mocks have not digested him — in a 12-team room he is a target in the 20s, not at 11

This league pays 0.1 per rush attempt — a 300-carry back banks 30 points before a single yard. Note the direction of drift this week: the volume backs all cooled slightly (Jonathan Taylor 7.3→7.6, James Cook III 14.5→15.3, Derrick Henry 15.6→16.1, Saquon Barkley 18.2→18.8, Omarion Hampton 19.4→20.0) while pass-catching Chase Brown rose 13.7→12.3. The market is moving away from exactly the profile this scoring rewards

The board plays about 14 picks deeper than ADP suggests. Twelve team defenses sit inside FFC's top 192 (Denver 95.9 through Tennessee 160.5) and two more by rank 204 — none will be drafted here, because no DEF slot exists. Pick 190 is effectively FFC rank ~204, and every late-round target comes off roughly a round later than its ADP implies

Dead picks at current ADP: Ricky Pearsall is still going at 107.4 despite season-ending PCL surgery with a six-to-twelve-month timeline — he is on IR and will not play in 2026. Brandon Aiyuk and Tyreek Hill have fallen out of FFC's top 239 entirely. James Conner 156.3 on 11 drafts is a name with no role. Kenyon Sadiq 159.0 after this week's hernia-recovery setback

Tight end got cheaper this week, which matters because league_average_match is on and every team also plays the weekly median: Trey McBride 34.2→35.2, Brock Bowers 38.9→40.7, Colston Loveland 58.8→61.1, Tyler Warren 64.8→66.7, Sam LaPorta 83.7→88.4, Harold Fannin Jr. 76.8→80.2. Kyle Pitts Sr. is the lone riser at 80.9→78.9

Late-round risers still worth the price: Jonathon Brooks 120.8→117.2, Quentin Johnston 97.2→94.1 as the clear WR2 behind Ladd McConkey under Mike McDaniel, Rachaad White 100.5→98.0 on a career 51-reception average in full PPR. Deebo Samuel Sr. 101.9 with a 16.9 standard deviation — back in San Francisco on a one-year deal and the direct beneficiary of Pearsall's loss; the wide range means he is gettable well past his ADP

PROVISIONAL: the draft's draft_order is still null, so slot 3 comes from config, not from Sleeper. If it holds, picks land at 3, 22, 27, 46, 51, 70, 75, 94, 99, 118, 123, 142, 147, 166, 171, 190. Re-confirm once the commissioner randomizes

CHANGED — Round 1 (pick 3). Bijan signing removes the scenario the plan was built around; he is no longer falling. The realistic board at 3 is Puka Nacua 2.7 or Ja'Marr Chase 3.9, with Jahmyr Gibbs 1.6 as the one upside break if a manager fades the hold-in. Order: Gibbs if he is somehow there, then Chase, then Nacua. Chase over Nacua at equal ADP tier — Nacua carries unresolved discipline exposure and the league has not priced it

The 3-to-22 wrap is 18 picks and it will consume the entire workhorse tier. Eleven backs carry an ADP inside pick 21: Gibbs 1.6, Bijan 2.0, McCaffrey 5.3, Jonathan Taylor 7.6, De'Von Achane 9.4, Chase Brown 12.3, Ashton Jeanty 13.8, James Cook III 15.3, Derrick Henry 16.1, Saquon Barkley 18.8, Omarion Hampton 20.0. Do not plan on a second true workhorse at 22 — if you want two, the RB has to be the pick at 3

CHANGED — Rounds 2-3 (22, 27) is the WR-volume window, and with three WR starters plus a FLEX in full PPR, take two. Available range: Chris Olave 20.2, George Pickens 21.3, Nico Collins 23.1, Zay Flowers 26.5 (now paid, $35M/yr, no contract question), Breece Hall 28.0, Garrett Wilson 28.2, DeVonta Smith 28.9. Nabers is no longer part of this window — his rise to 34.8 pushes him to the 46 pick, and he is the best value there if he lasts

Rounds 4-5 (46, 51) is the TE decision point, and the tier came to you this week. McBride 35.2 and Bowers 40.7 will be gone; Colston Loveland 61.1, Tyler Warren 66.7, Kyle Pitts Sr. 78.9 and Harold Fannin Jr. 80.2 all now sit past pick 55, meaning you can take Malik Nabers 34.8 or Emeka Egbuka 33.8 at 46 and still get a starting TE at 70. Because every team also plays the weekly median, take the higher-floor tight end over the athletic upside swing

Wait on QB until 70-99. The range there: Dak Prescott 67.1, Jayden Daniels 71.1, Jalen Hurts 75.0, Brock Purdy 81.5, Matthew Stafford 83.8, Trevor Lawrence 89.2, Patrick Mahomes 96.6. Spending pick 22 or 27 on Josh Allen (26.4) is a 40-to-70-pick premium at the one position where a single starter plays and pass TDs are worth 4

Kicker at 190 and not one pick earlier. Brandon Aubrey at 130.0 is inflated by rooms that also draft defenses; Jason Myers 140.1, Ka'imi Fairbairn 142.5, Jake Bates 143.8, Cameron Dicker 146.4, Harrison Mevis 151.1 and Cam Little 163.3 are all reachable in the final round. And there is no team-defense slot in this league at all — never draft one, at any price

KEEPER — STILL UNRESOLVED, and it is now the only gap in the plan. Sleeper's /rosters endpoint for the 2025 league (1257482480479379456) is outside this task's fetch allowlist, so there is no candidate list. Run this once and the recommendation becomes concrete: curl -s "https://api.sleeper.app/v1/league/1257482480479379456/rosters" | python3 -m json.tool. Framework meanwhile: max_keepers is 1. If the keeper costs the round-1 pick, only a player in the Nacua/Chase tier (top ~5 ADP) clears the bar. If it costs a later pick, any top-40 ADP asset clears it easily

NEW — the biggest injury of the weekend is on a line, not at a skill spot: Commanders LT Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps in Saturday's practice, beaten on a bull rush by Odafe Oweh in one-on-ones. Surgery is required and the reporting (ESPN, NFL Network, 8/8-8/9) is that he misses most, if not all, of 2026 — typical recovery is four to seven months. Washington made him the first $30M-per-year offensive lineman five months ago. Everything in that offense gets marked down a notch: fade the Commanders' passing-game pieces at ADP rather than paying up

NEW — Las Vegas held QB Kirk Cousins and EDGE Maxx Crosby out of all team drills Saturday as discipline for a fight at Friday's practice. Klint Kubiak: "We have very clear expectations about how we want to practice, how you go about our business. We violated that yesterday, so we held those guys out." Rookie Fernando Mendoza took his first first-team reps of camp and threw touchdowns to Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer and Tre Tucker. This is the Raiders QB battle cracking open — a live concern for anyone paying Bowers' 40.7 ADP at TE

NEW — Cleveland's QB competition tilted Saturday and not in the direction anyone expected. Todd Monken said before practice that Shedeur Sanders would take the majority of first-team reps; Deshaun Watson then took all of them and had one of his best days of camp, with a team spokesman saying Monken wanted to see Watson with certain personnel groups (Scott Petrak, NBC Sports, 8/8). The two had alternated through the first nine practices. Sanders took zero first-team snaps. Nothing to act on yet, but the Browns pass catchers' outlook moves with this

NEW — one-on-one drills claimed two more: Bills RB Ty Johnson grabbed his right knee during a pass-pro rep Saturday and was helped to the locker room limping, and Texans RB Jawhar Jordan is out with a hip. Seahawks RB Jadarian Price is expected back soon. None of the three is a draft target in a 16-round room, but Johnson's absence concentrates Buffalo's passing-down backfield work

ONGOING — Malik Nabers is still trending toward a Week 1 return (RotoWire, 8/9). No change from Friday's read, and no new practice restriction has been reported. He remains the best value at the 46 pick if he lasts past 40

ONGOING — the PUP board is unchanged from Friday and still the cleanest read on early-season availability. Zach Charbonnet (SEA, knee) is on reserve/PUP and misses a minimum of four games with a mid-season return anticipated; George Kittle (SF, Achilles) and Alec Pierce (IND, ankle) remain on their teams' lists. Charbonnet's absence is the one with a direct draft consequence — it collapses the Seattle committee to two backs for the first month

NEW — Josh Downs was the most glaring absence from Saturday's Day 8 practice, and the Colts confirmed it is a groin injury. No extent and no timetable were offered (Nathan Brown, IndyStar; NBC Sports, 8/8). That puts three receivers out at once: Downs (groin), Alec Pierce (PUP, ankle) and Laquon Treadwell (hamstring). Ashton Dulin, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and Anthony Gould worked as the first-team wideouts in their place

CHANGE — walk back Friday's Pierce optimism. NBC's Saturday write-up has Steichen saying earlier in the week that there is no timetable for Alec Pierce's return from PUP, which conflicts with the weekend PUP trackers still reporting he comes off within a week or so. Treat the Week 1 availability as genuinely unresolved rather than trending up

NEW — Day 8 (Saturday, Salute to Service, 95 minutes) went to the defense in the red-zone period: Laiatu Latu had a sack and another pressure, Akeem Davis-Gaither a pass breakup plus a run stop on Jonathan Taylor, and Robert Carter Jr. intercepted Anthony Richardson Sr. On offense, Ashton Dulin had an early drop and then was the most productive receiver on the field, and Riley Leonard hit Coleman Owen for a touchdown (Joel A. Erickson, IndyStar)

CHANGE — the kicking competition has stopped being dead even. Blake Grupe went 5-for-6 Saturday, converting from 25, 33, 42, 50 and 54 and missing only from 58, after both kickers finished 8-for-10 earlier in the week. Spencer Shrader kicks Sunday and needs a matching day to stay level

NEW — Saturday's injury list is a hamstring outbreak. RB DJ Giddens, WR Laquon Treadwell, S Hunter Wohler and LB C.J. Allen all missed with hamstrings, and DL Tim Smith was out with an undisclosed issue. WR Eli Pancol returned after missing the previous couple of practices. Giddens is the one to file away — he is the back directly behind Taylor, and Allen is now missing time for the second straight week after opening camp on PUP

SCHEDULE and around the team: Day 9 was Sunday 8/9, then a joint practice at New England Tuesday 8/11 and the preseason opener at New England Thursday 8/13, with joint practices hosting Atlanta 8/19-8/20 and the home preseason game vs. the Falcons 8/22. Cuts to 53 are Aug. 30. Sauce Gardner called Steichen a top-three play-caller in the league, and Jim Bob Cooter gave his eight-practice evaluation of Anthony Richardson Sr. (Colts Wire, 8/8-8/9)
